title: "A common report for race and gender gaps"

description: "Weighted expected-risk evaluation of a common report and two fixed KRW cards."
---

A common report assigns one grade across race and gender contact gaps. Moving the race weight shows when a common report and KRW's two fixed cards beat withholding every pair.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **“Equal weights.”** At the default cost, the common report's risk .245 beats withholding every comparison, whereas both fixed KRW cards have higher risk.
- **“Race .80” and “Gender .80.”** The race card crosses the withholding line near race weight .69; the gender card crosses near .29.
- **Settings and firm details.** Switch the colored report, adjust the grade cap, or select any firm in the scatterplot or Data table to read both marginal intervals.

<details>
<summary>Live order search and archived comparison</summary>

The browser combines each firm's average posterior ranks with the current weights and searches cuts of the resulting order. At the original equal weights, cost, and cap, it reproduces the archived result from a search over all capped reports. Each published KRW card was chosen under its own objective; its risk here measures how that fixed card performs under the current loss.

</details>

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Separate race and gender fits give marginal intervals and expected losses for each gap; variation in the scatterplot is across firms, not a within-firm joint posterior. **These experimental data do not describe firms’ current conduct.** Data: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), doi:10.1257/aer.20230700; deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1, CC-BY-NC as stated by the deposit (no version), noncommercial use only; as adapted in postrank 1.1.0, changes noted. <details class="prx-recipe">
<summary>In postrank</summary>

This call loads the released analysis and evaluates both published cards under its common loss.

```r
library(postrank); source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package = "postrank"))
krw <- load_or_compute("case_krw_signed97"); cards <- pr_case_krw$reference$single_criterion$grade
postrank_compare(krw, race_card = cards$race, gender_card = cards$gender, baselines = character())$table
```
</details>

Standalone: [embed/krw-two.html](../../embed/krw-two.html), for example `?w=.8&report=race`.
